source.title: Vorticity and Regularity for Viscous Incompressible Flows under the Dirichlet Boundary Condition. Results and Related Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes initial-boundary value problem in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ with the no-slip boundary condition u|_{∂Ω} = 0, suppose that whenever the vorticity at two points is larger than a fixed threshold K, the angle θ(x,y,t) between the two vorticity vectors satisfies either the 1/2-Hölder coherence bound sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|^{1/2} or even the stronger Lipschitz bound sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|. Is either of these geometric assumptions on the vorticity direction sufficient to guarantee that the solution stays regular?

evidence.quote: Open Problem. Consider the problem (2.1), (2.12) with Ω = R3+. Is the assumption (2.4) (or even(2.2)) sufficient to guarantee the regularity of the solution?
In particular, (2.4) alone is a sufficient condition for regularity.

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations under suitable boundary conditions, are weak solutions unique, and do strong solutions remain global in time rather than existing only on a short initial interval?

evidence.quote: It may be superfluous to recall that it is not known whether weak solutions are unique and whether strong solutions are global in time.
These are among the most important and challenging open problems in mathematics.

accepted.question_text: Consider the geometric regularity criterion for three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes flows that, at points x and y where both vorticity magnitudes exceed a fixed threshold K, the angle θ(x,y,t) between the two vorticity vectors obeys sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|^β. Can one prove regularity for some exponent β smaller than 1/2 without imposing any additional hypothesis beyond this geometric condition?

evidence.quote: The central and more challenging open problem is the improvement of the best exponent β for which the assumption (2.9) guarantees the regularity of the solutions without any other additional hypotheses.
Let β ∈ [0, 1/2] and assume that, for a.a. t ∈ (0,T), sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x − y|β (2.9)
In [5] Berselli and the author improve the above result by showing that sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x − y|1/2 (2.4) is sufficient to guarantee the regularity of weak solutions.

accepted.question_text: Can the regularity theory based on geometric coherence of the vorticity direction for the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations be extended from the whole-space case to boundary value problems, especially to problems with physical boundary conditions rather than no boundary at all?

evidence.quote: A main open problem is the extension of the above type of results to boundary value problems.
Another central problem is the extension of the basic theory to boundary value problems.

accepted.question_text: Under the no-slip (Dirichlet) boundary condition for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, can one control the additional boundary term created by the combination of viscosity and adherence strongly enough to deduce regularity from the vorticity-direction criterion, for example by proving an estimate of the form shown in (2.15)?

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, without further hypotheses, we are not able now to extend to the non slip (or adherence) boundary condition the 1/2-Hölder sufficient condition. This is not due to the “nonlinear” term (ω ·∇)u·ω but to a boundary integral which is due to the combination of viscosity and adherence to the boundary.

The new obstacle is due to the “additional” boundary integral that appears on the left-hand side of equation (3.2). This term is due to the combination of viscosity and adherence to the boundary, and not to the nonlinear term.
If, in addition, an upper bound of the form ... (2.15) holds ... then u is regular in ]0,T].
